comments.author: miellaby

comments.author: peterBlue75

There’s more to come. disclaimer: I‘m part of the training team

comments.author: tomComb
comments.text: For a post to make such a big deal about sovereignty it is a bit misleading to not mention that the company is slated to be merged with Cohere, a Canadian company. And that is a good thing - no need to hide it. Given the growing cost of keeping up, these few non-US, non-Chinese companies really need to do more sharing of efforts and costs. Canada too is very much in need of sovereign AI options, but funding that on its own would be pretty much a waste of money. Would love to see this new German Canadian company cooperate with Mistral too, or maybe one of the Korean AI companies.

comments.author: niemandhier
comments.text: I think at the moment the main thing a sovereign AI model needs to be good at is auditing the results of other models. Right now one could run an open model for most government applications and it would be good enough, you just cannot trust any of these. So having a sovereign controlled model audit the first one would basically act like a “trust adapter”. If the second model is cheap and fast enough, there is a business model. You don’t even need to audit all the intermediate steps, just tool calls and end results.

Instead, it's compared with Qwen3-Next 80B-A3B, a model released almost a full year ago. I get that doesn't invalidate the real "point" of the model, but...

stories.summary_ja: 主な議論点は、Aleph Alphaが公開したKolibriの透明性とチュートリアル形式の論文、データセット開示、そして英語・ドイツ語でコーディングやエージェントタスクでも良好な性能を示す点だった。さらに、1年未満のチームによる初リリースであり、イテレーション速度を重視していることも注目された。一方、主権的AIを謳う一方で、社が近くカナダのCohereと合併予定であることを指摘し、主権主張が誤解を招くとの批判や、非米中企業間でのコスト共有・協力の必要性が議論された。また、Kolibriを他モデルの出力監査（「トラストアダプター」）として活用し、ビジネスモデルにできるという見方や、Qwen3.8 Flashとの比較が欠けていることへの指摘も見られた。
stories.editor_note: KolibriはAleph Alphaがドイツ語・英語に特化したオープンウェイトLLMで、EUのデータ主権論議が高まる中、ローカルでの高精度言語処理への期待が集まっている。日本でも同様に国内データ利用のニーズが高まる点で注目される。

comments.author: sigbottle
comments.text: What does "OS" for clouds mean? Does this mean you still delegate to something like KVM/paravirtualzation for your device models, but your FTL guest OS can run multiple secure workloads inside a VM? Or are you designing a custom OS from the ground up to run on native hardware? What constraints are you putting on hardware support to make this a tractable that's not re-implementing all of the stuff that linux has? I assume that's why it's advertised for the "cloud", because you know a priori the deployment machines you're gonna run on? Or is hardware support known by kernel devs to be a (relatively) trivial problem in the OS space, compared to the user-facing features (like processes, scheduling, memory management, etc)? Or is the bet that microkernel = win = can implement everything linux has and more? I'm curious about the eventual end goal for the project is, not just what currently exists (as otherwise the answer currently seems to be sentence 1)

stories.summary_ja:
主な議論点: FTLが本格的なクラウドOSとして成長できるか、ホビープロジェクトか、コンテナが独自カーネルを不要にする点、ハードウェア抽象化の範囲、マイクロカーネル戦略の有効性など。  
賛否両論: 支持側は、Rustベースの非同期ランタイムとLinux互換層がクラウドワークロードに軽量で安全だと評価。懐疑側は、ハードウェアドライバや既存エコシステムの再実装コストが大きく、ホビーレベルを超えるのは難しいと指摘。  
注目コメント: 「コンテナは実際には独立カーネルを必要とせず、FTLは chroot jail に近づけるだけで十分」という指摘が、OSの役割を最小限に抜く設計哲学を示しており、他の議論の焦点となった。さらに、カーネル以外の機能をユーザースペースに移すことで、セキュリティ境界が明確になるという利点も指摘された。
stories.editor_note: FTLはクラウドインフラ向けに設計された新OSで、コンテナやマイクロサービスのオーバーヘッドを削減し、ベアメタル級の性能を狙う。日本のクラウドベンダーが自社スタック最適化に動く中、参考になるアーキテクチャだ。

stories.title_en: Woking Electrical Control Room (2016)
stories.title_ja: ウォーキング電気制御室(2016)

comments.author: intrasight
comments.text: There is so much cool tech and tech spaces that have been lost in terms of the visual history and story. I wish I could go back in time and capture more of the spaces and artifacts that I was involved in. Perhaps this isn't an issue for anything created in the last 15 years since smartphones have existed.

comments.author: SoftTalker
comments.text: Misread the title as "Working" control room, and was ready to be amazed that something like that from the first half of the last century was still in use... and not even a PC or screen to be found. But, it was decomissioned in 1997. Really interesting how depression-era infrastructure like that was still built with so much attention to aesthetic design. Today it would just be screens on a wall, industrial carpet floor, drop-tile ceiling with LED lights, a few Steelcase cubicles for the operators and little else.

comments.author: footydude
comments.text: There's something very beautiful about the attention to detail and forethought that has gone into rooms like this. The wonderful combination of beauty through a clear focus on functionality, supported by just enough of a sense of majesty to lift the whole space beyond pure functionality makes it a little more special. This is probably a place that was always considered at least somewhat beautiful given its strong design, but more generally speaking I find it really interesting seeing how functional ~1930-1970s era industrial units like this have kinda become fascinating and (in their own way) beautiful places in the eyes of so many (me included). I often wonder how people in the future will look back at our current humdrum infrastructure and what they might think of it. No doubt there'll be just as much nostalgia and fascination in some quarters, but i have to admit it's a little hard at times for me to see what elements of modern infrastructure will become the focal point of curious minds in, say, the 2050s. That said, I did visit a museum last year that had some pylon insulators and some other old 1990s electric-grid equipment and I found it kinda interesting and beautiful in its own way so what do I know?!

comments.author: adonovan
comments.text: I was wondering whether it was still in use, and if so for how much longer. Apparently it is no longer operational but, hearteningly, has been historically preserved and is now let out as a period filming location. https://filming.networkrail.co.uk/filming-locations/woking-e...

comments.author: actinium226

stories.summary_ja:
主な議論点: コミュニティは、1930‑1970年代の電気制御室の美しいデザインと機能性の融合に注目し、当時のインフラが現在では失われつつある視覚的・物語的遺産であると指摘。また、その施設が1997年に稼働停止後、歴史的に保存され撮影場所として活用されている事実にも関心が集まった。  
賛否両論: 多くの参加者が当時の装飾的な細部への称賛とノスタルジーを共有する一方、現代のインフラ（スクリーンや工業用カーペットなど）が将来同様に価値ある遺産と見なされるか疑問を呈する意見もあり、過去と現在の評価基準の違いが議論の分かれ目となった。  
注目コメント: 「当時の美しさは機能のための美であり、今日の単調な設備とは対照的」という指摘が特に洞察的であり、さらに「この部屋はビデオゲームに登場しそうな雰囲気」というコメントが視覚的インスピレーションとして注目された。

stories.title_en: City building games have a Soul Problem pt.2
stories.title_ja: シティビルディングゲームにはソウル問題がある パート2

comments.author: stillpointlab
comments.text: I recall working on a sports game where they hired a new art director who had previously worked in Hollywood on visual effects for movies. One of my coworkers had a meeting where the new art director requested that the player's uniforms have cloth simulation in the dynamic cut scenes. It was then necessary to explain the difference between pre-rendered scenes and real-time rendering budgets. It often isn't a question about whether or not something can be done. In pre-rendered scenes, or screenshots, the budget is very different than in game. At whatever target frame-rate you choose, there is a finite amount of visual effects you can achieve. Spending that budget requires compromise. It's easy to live in a fantasy world where you can demand no compromise. The hard thing is doing the most you possibly can given very real budgets and doing so with the people you have available. Not every studio is Rockstar with the ability to throw unlimited devs for several years at the problem.

comments.author: card_zero
comments.text: The problem might be getting people to negotiate stairs smoothly. The Sims (up to version 3, anyway) didn't want to deal with collisions on stairs, there's no animation for squeezing past or turning around, so Sims approaching stairs spend a lot of time slowly getting out of one another's way to decide who's going to use the stairs first, and waiting for other Sims to finish so that the next Sim can embark. If you throw a party in a house with stairs, some guests can spend the entire time stuck in the stair queue, and then they go home and complain that the party was no fun.

comments.author: db48x
comments.text: He is partly correct, but forgets about the polygon budget. The GPU is fast but not infinitely so. It has lots of texture memory, but not an infinite amount. Game developers have to balance graphical fidelity against the rendering time. They actually did a really bad job of this for Cities: Skylines 2 and it was a big reason why the game was so sluggish on release. Search for the story of the teeth for a particularly salient example. Also that grand staircase should be something the player chooses to place, rather than something you get every time a path is sloped.

comments.author: matheusmoreira
comments.text: > Does this look nice to you? Yes, it does. It's exactly what I want my real life city to be like. No plants growing everywhere completely out of control and invading perimeters they aren't supposed to be in. No cracked pavement that's just a rainfall away from being replaced with potholes. Apparently, "soul" means a city that looks like it's unmaintained and teetering on the edge of a precipice, just about to be reclaimed by nature, a few years away from turning into the green urbanscape of The Last of Us.

comments.author: kajman
comments.text: Cities: Skylines 2 is a particularly rough pick for this concept, since it's one of very few games I need frame generation to run even passably. LLMs seem plenty capable of tweaking existing assets to make a ton of variants, but actually displaying all of those performantly is then an engineering problem. And without many variants, things like "splotchy wall apartment building" would get old so much faster when there's several square blocks of them instead of bizarrely pristine ones.

stories.summary_ja: 主な議論点: 「ソウル」とは何かという議論。ビジュアルの豊かさ（衣服シミュレーション、歯のモデル、階段など）とリアルタイムレンダリングの予算・GPU制約のトレードオフが中心。賛否両論: 詳細を追加すれば没入感が高まるという意見と、フレームレート低下や不具合を招くため最適化が必要という意見が分かれた。注目コメント: GPUのテクスチャ・ポリゴン予算に言及し、Cities: Skylines 2の歯モデル例や階段はプレイヤーが選べるべきだと指摘したコメントが特に洞察的だった。さらに、シムズの階段待ちやスポーツゲームでのクロスシリウス要求など、具体的な事例が挙げられ、理想と実装コストのギャップが論じられた。
stories.editor_note: シティビルディングゲームの「ソウル問題」Part2は、プレイヤーの創造意欲が単なる最適化に置き換わるジレンマを指摘。日本のシムシティファンがModで物語性を求める傾向と共鳴する。

They seem to be much smarter than we gave them credit for all the way to the unfortunately named dodo bird and its old inaccurate depiction that took hold in public conscience. Now apparently they have an similar thing to our proprioception(tho hard to tell if as accurate as ours) if I'm understanding the abstract correctly.

stories.summary_ja:
・主な議論点  
コミュニティでは、ゴフィンコカトウ（Goffin’s cockatoo）における身体認識テスト（BAO: Body Awareness Orientation）の適用可能性と、鳥類全般の認知能力についての議論が中心となった。特に、鏡や簡易な操作課題を用いて鳥が自己の身体位置や動作をどのように認識できるか、およびその結果が従来の「鳥脳」という偏見をどのように覆すかが話題になった。

・賛否両論  
賛成側は、過去のカラス研究や今回の実験結果から、鳥類が高度な空間認識や自己認識を持つ可能性が高いと指摘し、BAOテストを家庭の鳥でも試す価値があると肯定的だった。一方で、一部のコメントでは、鳥の行動が単なる条件反射や学習に過ぎず、真の身体認識（プロ prioception）と同等であるかはまだ断定できないという懐疑的意見も見られ、実験デザインの厳密さや解釈の範囲について意見が分かれた。

・注目コメント  
あるユーザーは「自分家のコヌルでもBAOテストを試してみたい」と述べ、鏡や簡易な操作具を用いた自宅での観察計画を共有した。このコメントは、学術的な知見を日常のペット飼育に結びつけようとする実践的な関心を示しており、鳥類の認知研究への一般市民の関与を促す点で特に洞察があったと評価された。
stories.editor_note: ゴフィンオウムの身体認識研究は、鳥類でも自己身体マップが存在することを示し、認知科学の進化論的視点を提供。日本のロボット研究者が動物の身体 schema を参考にした柔軟制御に興味を持つ。

stories.editor_note: C++ Insightsはコンパイラの視点でテンプレート展開や暗黙変換を可視化し、コードの本当の挙動を学べる。日本のエンジニアがC++20以降の複雑機能を安全に使うための学習ツールとして重宝される。

comments.author: iamwil
comments.text: I remember playing a crap web game in college, kinda like gunslinger, where you try to shoot people who turn around with a gun (and not those without). When I graduated college, Ian--one of my good friends at work--ended up being one of those guys in the game! Turns out that game I was playing was built by Tom Fulp, and he was using his friends (like Ian) as characters in his games pre-Newgrounds. All that messing around with crap games on the internet paid off. He had started Newgrounds while in college, and had quit to do it. Met Tom once, and he was a cool guy, but he didn't believe in the stuff that they taught in CS. He had a long rant about how learning string diff algorithms were useless. Anyway, it turns out later on, he went back to college to finish his degree. When his classmate(s) found out who he was, this one kid was so excited to sit next to him. A “gateway” sits between the relay and app server to handle all of this cryptography — decapsulating requests, encapsulating responses — and the app server handles only plain HTTP Wouldn't that be better if you design an oblivious encryption method so the encryption and decryption is handled by the origin server (a.k.a Target Resource in the RFC) and the Client? stories.summary_ja: 主な議論点は、OHTTP（Oblivious HTTP）が提供するプライバシー保護の実用性と、Cloudflareが中継ギャウェイとして果たす役割への信頼度である。コメントでは、OHTTPがクライアントとアプリサーバーだけが平文を見られ、中継は暗号文のみを見る仕組みだと説明され、これがIPアドレスの露出を防ぎ、オフラインアプリのアップデートチェックなどに有用だと指摘された。一方で、Cloudflareがインターネットトラフィックの半分を仲介しているため、大きなテック企業と同様に中央集権的な信頼問題が残り、「単なる匿名SOCKS5と変わらない」という批判も出た。賛否両論として、プライバシー志向の開発者はOHTTPを歓迎し、私的ソフトウェアやBiscottiのようなプライバシー中心のアナリティクスへの適用を期待する声があるのに対し、中継をCloudflareに依存する点や、オリジンサーバー自身が暗号化／復号化を行う設計への改善提案が疑問視された。注目コメントは、OHTTPの暗号フローを詳しく解説し、中継ではなくオリジンサーバーで鍵管理を行うべきだと提案したものと、オフライン transcription ソフトウェアでの活用事例を挙げながら、実際に使いたかったという実務的な視点を示したものである。

comments.author: janalsncm
comments.text: > The algorithm also learned far faster—it played about 34 times fewer games than DeepNash, and still ended up much stronger. Imo, this is the critical piece and what makes the AI work at all. With hidden information games, the best move depends on information you don’t have. So a move could be good or bad, it just depends on something that’s impossible to know. You’d like to search ahead, meaning “if I do this they will do that” but that’s impossible since you don’t even know what the opponent can do because you don’t know their hidden state. If the possible hidden states are randomly distributed, you are screwed. It’s just like rock paper scissors: there’s no best move if your opponent is unpredictable. However if you can quickly learn to predict their moves, it becomes possible to make informed decisions about what to do.

In my case it silently broke migration for Aerial from 3.X to 4.X in Golden Gate (where I moved away from the legacyScreenSaver extension to the new undocumented wallpaperextension format). I did move to "/Users/Shared" earlier this year but some people will inevitably get caught by this if they didn't update, and there's no recourse, FDA doesn't work, you can't even ask for access, nothing works. あるコメントでは、「モデルはグレーダーに執着している。それは人間にとってのセックスに相当する進化的圧力だ」と指摘し、評価メカニズムがモデルの行動原理を根本から動かしているという洞察が注目された。また、別のユーザーは「AIが直接出力を生成するのではなく、創造のプロセス自体を学ばせることが本当の革新になるかもしれない」と述べ、出力重視からプロセス重視への paradigm shift の可能性を示唆した。

・主な議論点  
GLM 5.3 Flashのエネルギー消費が極めて低く、月間の利用コストがたった68ドル（約4kWh、365gCO₂）で、総コストの1%に過ぎない点が驚きと議論の中心となった。また、「9月いっぱいこれを使う」という挑戦が実際にはうまくいかなかったという体験談や、モデル選択ミスによるトークン・コストの急増、費用対効果を測るグラフの有用性についても話題になった。

・賛否両論  
エネルギー効率については「データセンターの過剰投資はファイバービルドのようになる」と楽観的見方と、実際の利用では思ったほど節約できずコストがかさむという批判が分かれた。モデル選択の失敗については「適切なモデルを選べば5分の1のコストで同等結果が得られた」という教訓に賛同する声と、失敗の具体例や根拠が不明瞭だと指摘する声が対立した。

・注目コメント  
「トークン単価だけでは比較できない；タスク完了時間や総コストを軸にしたAAのA Indexグラフが本当のパレト図になる」という指摘が、評価方法の改善点として特に洞察に富んでいた。また、投稿がLLM生成か疑問を呈し、失敗の具体例を求める声も注目された。
